analysis_notes.source_text_analysis: Torah #99 (LM2) is an extremely brief three-sentence aggadic saying, not a structured analytical Torah. The Rebbe describes the ideal of hitbodedut (personal prayer/seclusion): pouring out one's speech before God so intensely that one's soul nearly departs from the body, hanging by a thread due to grief, longing (gaaguim), and desire (kisufim). He supports this with the Talmudic teaching (Taanit 8a) that prayer is only heard when one places one's soul in one's palm — equating that Talmudic state with the hitbodedut ideal ('hainu kannul'). He concludes that when God helps in hitbodedut, the experience becomes like a person speaking to a friend. The text uses no explicit bechina language ('X הוא בחינת Y'). The only equation present is an implicit one: הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת and תְּפִלָּה are treated as the same state ('hainu kannul'), but this is not expressed with structural bechina terminology. No bechina edges exist in the dataset for reference 1099. The source text does not support extracting any formal bechina packages.
